info.terms.title: Terms
info.privacy.title: Privacy
info.help.title: Help & feedback
info.tips.title: Safe handover tips
info.terms.0.title: A little campus teamwork
info.terms.0.body: Zarqa is a student-made lost-and-found service for the GUtech community. It isn't run by GUtech and isn't an official university channel, though the GUtech RSA desk helps with items handed in there. Using Zarqa means you agree to these terms and to the Privacy notice.
info.terms.1.title: Who can use it
info.terms.1.body: You need to be 18 or older and sign in with your own GUtech email. If you're under 18, hand in or ask about items at the RSA desk in person instead. One account per person, and keep your sign-in codes to yourself.
info.terms.2.title: Keep it honest
info.terms.2.body: Only post things you really lost or found, and only share photos and details you have the right to share. Don't claim someone else's property, pretend to be someone else, harass anyone or post unlawful content. Oman's laws apply, including the Cyber Crime Law. We may close reports or suspend accounts that break these rules, and may report serious misuse to GUtech or the authorities.
info.terms.3.title: A match is a suggestion
info.terms.3.body: AI can miss items or suggest the wrong one. Check identifying details before handing anything over. Zarqa doesn't hold items (only the RSA desk does, for things handed in there), verify ownership, guarantee a return or arrange the handover for you. Meet safely and never pay to unlock a match.
info.terms.4.title: No guarantees
info.terms.4.body: Zarqa is free and run by a student, as it is. It may change, pause or stop. As far as the law allows, we aren't responsible for lost, damaged or wrongly returned items, or for what happens when users meet.
info.terms.5.title: Changes, leaving and the law
info.terms.5.body: If these terms or the Privacy notice change in a way that matters, Zarqa asks you to agree again before you carry on. You can leave any time: close your reports or delete your account in Profile. These terms are governed by the laws of the Sultanate of Oman. Questions or a report of misuse: email us below.
info.privacy.0.title: Who's responsible
info.privacy.0.body: Zarqa is run by a GUtech student (the operator), who is responsible for your data (the data controller) and also acts as its data protection officer. Zarqa isn't run by GUtech. For any privacy question or request, email hello@tryzarqa.com.
info.privacy.1.title: What we collect
info.privacy.1.body: Your university email, first name, profile settings and optional avatar; your lost and found reports, their photos, match results and matching logs; and chats, handover details and read markers. Uploaded photos are re-encoded with their location and camera data (EXIF) removed. Sign-in uses one session cookie and short-lived sign-in codes. If you turn on push alerts, we store your browser's push subscription. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking cookies.
info.privacy.2.title: Why we use it
info.privacy.2.body: Only to run the lost-and-found: to sign you in, match lost and found reports, let owners and finders talk and arrange handovers, work with the RSA desk, send you the emails and alerts the service needs, and keep it safe from misuse. We never sell your data and never send marketing or advertising.
info.privacy.3.title: Your consent
info.privacy.3.body: We use your data because you expressly agree to it. Zarqa asks for that consent, and records when you gave it and to which version, before you can use the service. That includes processing outside Oman (see below). You can withdraw consent at any time by deleting your account in Profile or emailing us. Zarqa is for people aged 18 or older. If RSA desk staff file a report for you at your request, Zarqa asks for your consent when you first sign in.
info.privacy.4.title: Who can see it?
info.privacy.4.body: There is no public list of reports. Possible matches are shown to the person who lost the item, and a confirmed match opens a private chat between owner and finder. Ordinary photos can be shown with a match. Photos of cards and IDs are first covered on our own server by text recognition (OCR) that hides every number, machine-readable line and barcode it finds; names, faces and logos stay visible. Only that covered copy is ever shown: to a possible owner while they decide, to the finder or owner after a claim, to RSA staff and to admins. If covering fails or any number is still readable, the photo stays visible only to its uploader, and the original is never shown to anyone else. Admins can see reports, owner emails, photos (card photos only covered) and matching logs to moderate the service, and the operator has server access for maintenance. GUtech RSA desk staff can read owner–finder chats (read-only, to keep handovers safe) and see every found report with its photos and the finder's first name (if shown); when someone claims an item at the desk they also see the owner's first name and description. If you ask for an item at the desk, staff can file a lost report for you under your GUtech email.
info.privacy.5.title: Processing outside Oman
info.privacy.5.body: Zarqa needs providers outside Oman to work. Our server is hosted by Contabo in Europe. OpenAI (United States) reads report text and permitted photos to find matches; DeepSeek (China) and TypeSafe step in only when the main AI is unavailable. Resend (United States) sends our emails, and your browser's push service delivers alerts you turn on. Original card and ID photos never go to any provider: the covering runs on our own server. We chose providers we believe protect data to a standard comparable to Oman's law. Please don't write identity numbers, bank details, or health or other sensitive details in reports.
info.privacy.6.title: How long?
info.privacy.6.body: Open reports expire after 60 days without an update. Finished reports (returned, expired or closed), their photos and chats are deleted about six months (182 days) after that. Matching logs are kept for up to 182 days, even after you delete your account. Accounts stay until you delete them. Cleanup runs daily, so removal isn't instant. Nightly server backups are kept for 14 days. Found items handed in at the RSA desk stay listed until the RSA closes them, because the item is still on their shelf.
info.privacy.7.title: Your rights
info.privacy.7.body: Under Oman's Personal Data Protection Law you can withdraw your consent; ask us to correct, update or block your data; get a copy of it; have it sent to another provider; and have it deleted. Most of this you can do in the app: edit reports and profile, or use Profile › Delete my account, which removes your account, reports, photos, chats and alerts from the live service. For anything else, email us: we reply within 45 days, free of charge. If you think your data was handled unlawfully, you can complain to the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (linked below).
info.privacy.8.title: Keeping it safe
info.privacy.8.body: Connections are encrypted (HTTPS), the server is locked down to the operator, and backups can be read only by the operator. Only the people described above can see your data. If a breach puts your data at risk, we'll tell the Ministry and you within 72 hours of finding out, with what happened and what we're doing about it.
info.privacy.9.title: Changes to this notice
info.privacy.9.body: If this notice changes in a way that matters, Zarqa asks for your consent again before you carry on. This version is dated 13 November 2026.
info.help.0.title: Lost something?
info.help.0.body: Post a lost report from Home. Add the brand, colour, identifying marks and where and when you last had it. Zarqa looks for possible matches; check My reports and enable match alerts in Profile. Matching may be unavailable during the pilot.
info.help.1.title: Found something?
info.help.1.body: Post a found report. You can keep the item and meet the owner: when someone confirms a match, a chat opens so you can check ownership and arrange a handover. Or switch on “I'll drop it at the RSA desk”, take it there and show your drop code; the owner collects it from the RSA with a pickup code, no chat needed. Mark 'Got it back' only after the item has been returned.
info.help.2.title: Something feels off?
info.help.2.body: For a bug, mistaken claim, abusive message, privacy request or feedback, email hello@tryzarqa.com. Include a report reference if useful, but never send bank-card details, identity documents or sign-in codes. This inbox is not an emergency service.
info.tips.0.title: Meet where people are
info.tips.0.body: Choose a busy campus spot in daylight. Bring a friend if that feels better. Use chat to agree on a place and time, then confirm the handover.
info.tips.1.title: Check the little details
info.tips.1.body: Ask the claimant to describe a detail you have not shared, such as a sticker or what is inside a case. A match score is a clue, not proof of ownership.
info.tips.2.title: Keep private things private
info.tips.2.body: Do not share identity numbers, bank-card details, passwords or sign-in codes. For an ID or card, describe it without copying its numbers. Its uploaded photo is shown to others only with the numbers covered.
info.tips.3.title: No pressure, no payments
info.tips.3.body: Do not pay a fee or follow an unfamiliar link to claim an item. If something feels wrong, stop the handover and contact us. Once the item is safely back, tap 'Got it back' so Zarqa can stop searching.
